title: The well
hookLine: they drop him into a well, and Allah inspires him that one day he'll tell them what they did
carry: even in the well, a promise
tomorrow: The shirt and the false blood

cards: The brothers have their plan. Now they need their father to let the boy go. So they come to Ya'qub, all warmth.
Father, why don't you trust us with Yusuf? We only wish him well. Send him with us tomorrow; he'll run and play, and we'll look after him.
And Ya'qub says something that should chill them: it grieves me that you'd take him away, and I'm afraid a wolf might eat him while you're not paying attention. A wolf. He's handed them the words.
They answer: if a wolf eats him, with all of us there, we'd be losers indeed. In the morning, the boy goes out with them.

teach.h: THE WORST, IN A FEW WORDS.
teach.b: Surah Yusuf, verse fifteen, tells the worst moment in almost no words. So when they took him away, and agreed to put him in the depths of the well. That's it.
No struggle, no shouting, no boy's face. The Qur'an doesn't linger on the cruelty; it moves straight to what matters more.

And We inspired him: you will surely tell them about this deed of theirs, while they do not realize. A boy, maybe still a child, at the bottom of a dark, damp well, his brothers' voices fading overhead.
Into that darkness comes a message: this isn't the end. One day you'll stand in front of them and tell them what they did.
It doesn't take him out of the well, or stop the caravan, or the slavery, or the prison that's coming.

teach.h: A THREAD TO HOLD IN THE DARK.
teach.b: It gives him a thread to hold in the dark. And notice who it's for. Not the brothers; they don't hear it.
Not Ya'qub; he's at home, waiting. Just Yusuf, alone, where nobody else can reach.
The Arabic for the depths of the well is ghayabat al-jubb. Readers of the Arabic hear in ghayaba the root for what's hidden, unseen, the root of al-ghayb, the unseen world the Qur'an speaks of.

teach.h: EVEN IN THE WELL, A PROMISE.
teach.b: The bottom of the well is where you vanish from sight, and that's exactly where the promise reaches him. Some years later, and a few days from now for us, we'll see it kept.

how: Muslims often recite and reflect on Surah Yusuf in times of grief or hardship; the promise to Yusuf in the well is remembered as a sign that Allah reaches people where no one else can.

games.why: Allah inspired him: you will surely tell them about this deed of theirs, while they do not realize. a thread to hold in the dark.

practice: If you can, close your eyes or dim the light, and touch the edge of the darkest place you've been, or are in now; you don't need to relive it.
Then imagine that, even there, something reached you, a voice, a memory, a promise, a person, and if nothing did, imagine what you'd want to hear now.
If you pray, you can remember that Allah reached Yusuf at the bottom of the well.

wordCard.voice: The well. Where Yusuf's brothers left him, and where a promise found him: one day you'll tell them what they did. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 12:10 and 12:15: "the depths of the well" — from the root for hidden, unseen.
